sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: lob is a being of British folklore. The syllable lob forms part of many fairy names, much as the sound hob does in another set. A spirit called Lob-Lie-by-the-Fire was a great brownie who did hard work on a farm. He worked all day in spite of the lazy note in his name. The word lubber came down from the same root. People used it for a clumsy, foolish one who sat far from the busy world.
